filename: A Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Microphysical Properties of Ice Crystals From Cloud Particle Imagery.pdf
title: A Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Microphysical Properties of Ice Crystals From Cloud Particle Imagery
venue: Journal of Geophysical Research: Machine Learning and Computation
testbed_rationale: The synthetic particle image dataset is designed for computer vision estimation of single-crystal 3D geometric properties (effective density, area, bullet arm count) from 2D imagery, rather than training or evaluating atmospheric parameterization schemes or climate emulators directly.
pain_points: Ground truth 3D microphysical properties for in-situ cloud particle imager (CPI) observations are unavailable.
Real CPI images feature noise, out-of-focus artifacts, and optical resolution limits, while synthetic training data are idealized binary projections.
Idealized 3D models omit complex physical features such as hollowing of bullet arms and crystal surface irregularities.
Restricted to bullet rosette habit; multi-habit support requires broader synthetic generation and observational constraints.
extraction_notes: The research serves as a precursor to bottom-up constraints on mass-dimension (m-D) and area-dimension parameterizations in microphysics schemes, but the ML models themselves perform single-particle computer vision tasks.
